reading.title: Climate Change and Ocean Acidification
reading.passage: Ocean acidification occurs when excess carbon dioxide in the atmosphere dissolves into seawater, lowering its pH level. This phenomenon threatens marine ecosystems by weakening the shells of mollusks and corals. Scientists warn that if current emission rates continue, many shellfish populations may collapse within decades. The economic consequences are severe, as fishing industries and coastal communities depend heavily on marine resources. International cooperation is essential to reduce carbon emissions and protect ocean health for future generations.

questions.q: According to the passage, what happens when carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater?
questions.explanation: 지문에서 'dissolves into seawater, lowering its pH level'이라고 명시되어 있습니다. 따라서 정답은 B입니다.

questions.q: Which organisms are threatened by ocean acidification?
questions.explanation: 지문의 'weakening the shells of mollusks and corals'에서 연체동물과 산호가 위협받는다고 언급되어 있습니다.

questions.q: What is suggested as a necessary action to address this problem?
options: International cooperation to reduce carbon emissions
questions.explanation: 지문의 마지막 문장 'International cooperation is essential to reduce carbon emissions'에서 국제 협력이 필요하다고 명시되어 있습니다.

writing.prompt: Do you agree or disagree with the statement: 'Governments should prioritize environmental protection over economic development.' Support your opinion with specific examples.

structure.intro: 명확한 입장 제시. 예: 'I strongly agree that governments should prioritize environmental protection over economic development because...' (20-30단어)
structure.body1: 첫 번째 이유와 구체적 예시. 예: '첫째, 환경 보호는 장기적 경제 이익을 만든다. 예를 들어, 재생 에너지 산업은...' (60-80단어)
structure.body2: 두 번째 이유와 반론 대처. 예: '둘째, 환경 파괴의 비용이 경제 발전의 이익보다 크다. 예: 오염으로 인한 의료비...' (60-80단어)
structure.conclusion: 입장 재확인 및 미래 전망. 예: 'In conclusion, prioritizing environmental protection is not just ethical but economically wise for future generations.' (25-35단어)

speaking.prompt: Some people prefer to work in large corporations with many employees. Others prefer to work in small businesses or startups. Which do you prefer and why?
sample_points: 소규모 회사에서는 더 많은 책임과 다양한 경험을 할 수 있습니다. 예: 여러 프로젝트에 직접 관여하고 경영진과의 상호작용이 많습니다.
대규모 회사는 안정성, 복리후생, 경력 발전의 명확한 경로를 제공합니다. 예: 교육 기회, 퇴직금, 승진 시스템이 체계적입니다.

listening.title: Student and Professor Discussion About Research Methods
listening.script: Student: Professor, I'm confused about which research method to use for my project. Should I conduct interviews or surveys? Professor: That's a great question. It depends on your research goals. Interviews allow you to gather deep, detailed information from fewer people. You can explore complex topics thoroughly. Surveys, on the other hand, let you collect data from a larger population, which gives you more generalizable results. Student: So if I want to understand why people make certain decisions, interviews would be better? Professor: Exactly. Interviews are ideal for exploratory research. If you want to measure trends across a large group, surveys work better. You could also combine both methods for a more comprehensive study. Student: That makes sense. I think I'll start with interviews since I want to understand people's motivations.

questions.q: What is the main topic of this conversation?
questions.explanation: 학생이 인터뷰와 설문조사 중 어떤 방법을 사용할지 물어보고, 교수가 각 방법의 장점을 설명합니다. 따라서 주제는 '연구 방법 선택'입니다.

questions.q: According to the professor, what is an advantage of using interviews?
questions.explanation: 교수는 'Interviews allow you to gather deep, detailed information from fewer people'라고 명시했습니다. 인터뷰의 장점은 깊이 있는 정보 수집입니다.

questions.q: Why does the student decide to use interviews?
options: They want to understand people's motivations
They need data from a large group
questions.explanation: 학생이 'I want to understand people's motivations'라고 명확히 말했고, 이는 인터뷰가 탐색적 연구에 적합하기 때문입니다.
